answer: The tanner soaks his hides in pits he dug himself, and the currier counts the skins as they come out of the lime, because a hide cured in haste rots in the pit. Shepherd flock record with agriculture ministry attestation is the pit's patience that proves the work: six-year record, ear-tag registry, annual counts, veterinary visits. A hide cured with a stolen harbor rots in the pit and stinks out the yard. The trellis is the forfeit, the hides and the season's bark both paid to the yard's owner, and the pulse is the tan book, kept by the master tanner and read when the bark bills are settled.
